criteria.justification: The response directly cites that “a prior launch cleared [mapping accuracy] and still got paused because the output wasn't useful,” concluding that the proxy has already failed to predict customer value.

It explicitly identifies the year of investment and existing infrastructure as sunk costs and argues they justify reusing the work diagnostically, not retaining the engineering metric as the primary target.

The response squarely addresses the absence of ground truth, proposes several concrete sources and an interim expert-reconciled metric where outcomes lag, and recommends delaying launch if usable ground truth cannot be sourced in time.

It frames the primary metric as the team’s optimization “target” and contrasts optimizing against the old proxy with having a customer signal to optimize against, showing that metric choice will direct future work rather than merely score the launch.

It clearly recommends customer-facing estimate error as the primary launch gate, retains mapping accuracy as a diagnostic and non-regression guardrail, and lays out concrete pre-launch and post-launch transition steps.
